summary: Iteration 34 — exhaustive MOBILE (390x844) verification of the new native-app shell + PWA + touch UX + bottom-sheet modals across marketing, auth, dashboard, project overview/flow/document, public client review, settings; plus desktop regression at 1920x800. 32 checks executed → 31 pass, 1 real bug found & fixed by testing agent.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED by testing agent. /login (and any page using .hero-ambient) produced real horizontal scroll on mobile: document.documentElement.scrollWidth = 1198px (viewport 390px). Root cause: .hero-ambient sets overflow:visible with an absolutely-positioned ::before pseudo-element that is 1100px wide starting at left:20% — intended as a soft glow, but on a 390px viewport its right edge lands at ~1178px. html/body did not have overflow-x:hidden on mobile, so the bleed became scrollable. The scrollWidth was even growing over time (1201→1204→1207) because of the heroPulse animation's transform:scale(1.06). Fix: added `html, body { overflow-x: hidden; }` inside the existing @media (max-width: 768px) block (top of block, comment 0). Confirmed after fix: /login sw=390, / sw=390, /pricing sw=390, /faq sw=390, /how-it-works sw=390. Desktop untouched (sw=1920 at 1920px vp).

action_items: REVIEW my CSS fix: added `html, body { overflow-x: hidden; }` at the top of the existing @media (max-width:768px) block in /app/frontend/src/index.css (~line 3656). This is the standard mobile-safety pattern for pages that use decorative absolutely-positioned bleed elements (.hero-ambient, orbit backgrounds, etc.). Confirmed no regression on desktop (overflow-x hidden is scoped to mobile media query only). The alternative — clipping .hero-ambient itself — would remove the intended visual glow on marketing pages; the mobile clip is the correct trade.

OPTIONAL: consider adding a lightweight visual-regression check for scrollWidth<=clientWidth across all top-level routes at 390x844 as part of CI, since decorative-overflow bleed regressions are easy to reintroduce (any new absolute-positioned decoration without overflow-x guard could trip it).
critical_code_review_comments: The mobile CSS block was thoughtful (bottom sheets, 16px inputs, filter-tab swipe, tabbar safe-area) but missed the html/body overflow-x guard — a nearly-universal mobile CSS baseline. Any page mounting .hero-ambient (Landing, Login, most marketing pages) would have h-scrolled without it. Now fixed.

MobileTabBar.jsx: `onNew` scrolls the paste input into view even when user is already on /app (setTimeout 350ms fires regardless of route). Fine, but if the user is deep-scrolled in the projects list this yanks them back to hero without a visible cue — a small toast or focus-ring flash would soften it. Not a bug.

Login page has decorative .hero-ambient inside <main> with no wrapping container that clips — if the html/body overflow guard were ever removed, this would silently regress. Consider wrapping .hero-ambient parents with overflow:hidden as a belt-and-braces defence.

index.css is 3782 lines — approaching the 'split into modules' threshold. The new mobile block is at the tail and easy to lose; splitting into index.css + mobile.css (or Tailwind's @layer utilities) would help discoverability.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: /login (and any route that mounts <div class='hero-ambient'>) had real horizontal scroll on mobile because .hero-ambient sets overflow:visible with a pseudo-element ::before that is 1100px wide + heroPulse animation scaling it 1.06x. On a 390px viewport, the ::before's right edge falls at ~1178px, growing to ~1207px mid-animation. Neither html nor body had overflow-x:hidden on mobile, so the browser reported document.documentElement.scrollWidth=1198+ and enabled horizontal scrolling (touch swipe reveals empty background on the right). Reproduction: at viewport 390x844, load /login → swipe horizontally → page scrolls right. Fix applied by test agent: added `html, body { overflow-x: hidden; }` inside the existing MOBILE APP EXPERIENCE @media (max-width: 768px) block at index.css:3656. Verified across /, /login, /pricing, /faq, /how-it-works: all now report scrollWidth=390. Desktop viewport (1920px) reports scrollWidth=1920 (unchanged) since the rule is media-query scoped.
